hints: Look closely at Y and Z. Y has concentrated sucrose and Z has dilute sucrose, both surrounded by water and a partially permeable membrane. Where will water enter fastest by osmosis and build up the highest pressure?
Remember mass flow in a plant goes from source to sink in the phloem, with water returning in the xylem. Which plant organ makes lots of sucrose (source) and which uses it up (sink)?
walkthrough:
**Work out what happens in the model**

Think osmosis first. Water moves from the beaker into both bulbs, but much more water enters Y because it has concentrated sucrose and a very low water potential.

This builds high hydrostatic pressure at Y, which pushes solution along the top tube W toward Z, where pressure is lower.

**Match W and X to phloem and xylem**

The top tube W carries sugary solution under pressure from high to low pressure. That is exactly what the phloem sieve tube does.

The bottom tube X lets water flow back to balance the system. That represents the xylem returning water in the plant.

**Match Y and Z to leaves and roots**

Y is the high sucrose, high pressure end where loading happens. In a plant this is the source, the photosynthesizing leaves.

Z is the dilute sucrose, low pressure end where sucrose is removed. In a plant this is the sink, for example the roots. So flow along W is from Y to Z.

options.A: W as phloem and X as xylem is right, but Y as roots and Z as leaves is backwards. Y is the concentrated source so must be leaves.
options.B: W is phloem, X is xylem, Y is leaves (source), Z is roots (sink), with mass flow along W from Y to Z driven by high to low hydrostatic pressure.
options.C: W and X are swapped. The top pressure-flow tube W is phloem, not xylem, and the bottom return tube X is xylem, not phloem.
options.D: W and X are swapped. W is the phloem carrying sucrose from source to sink, so flow cannot be described as from Z to Y in this model.
